newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Air force incurs loss of 895 million rupees when it lost seven aircraft during a period of two years beginning August 1994, Education Minister Richard Pathirana tells parliament. 243 service personnel and six civilians were killed in these crashes.
A total of 634 civilians have been killed due to attacks by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) during a two year period beginning August 1994, Education Minister Pathirana tells parliament.
LTTE withdraws two camps north of Omanthai ahead of advancing troops. Troops on Operation "Jaya Sikuru" or "Sure of Victory" continue to push deeper into the rebels' northern Wanni stronghold.
Twenty two young LTTE cadres, who deserted the rebels recently, surrender to security forces in northern Jaffna peninusla.

Magistrate releases Lohan Ratwatte, son of senior government minister Anuruddha Ratwatte, and two other suspects due to lack of evidence to link them to last month's killing of Papua New Guinean rugby coach Joel Pera.
Air force says a fighter plane attacked a lorry carrying LTTE rebels at Mankulam in the Wanni region, killing at least 30 rebels.
Government launches programme to plant 1.5 million trees today to mark World Environment Day.
